title: Nonthermal Dynamics of a One-dimensional Rydberg-atom Chain with Constraint Four-body Interactions
abstract: We investigate dynamics of a linear chain of Rydberg atoms driven by a constrained four-body interaction, where two neighboring atoms are excited simultaneously from the electronic ground state $|0\rangle$ to Rydberg state $|1\rangle$ only when their closest neighbors are in $|0\rangle$ state. By employing an ansatz for the many-body ground state, the low-energy Hamiltonian is given by a tridiagonal form. The many-body ground state energy, which scales linearly with the chain length $L$, is obtained analytically in the thermodynamic limit and agrees with the one of the exact diagonalization. Our model supports quantum many-body scar eigenstates that are nearly equally spaced energetically. The scar states overlap strongly with the basis state $|\mathbf{0}\rangle=|0\cdots 0\rangle$. We show that the overlap distribution is tilted by the state-dependent four-body interaction. This leads to non-ergodic dynamics, evidenced by the revival of the initial state. The four-body constrained model can be realized with Rydberg atoms in a Peierls array with alternating bond lengths, where atoms on the shorter and longer bonds experience Rydberg blockade and antiblockade, respectively. Our study provides a pathway to explore constrained non-ergodic dynamics with four-body interactions by combining the Rydberg blockade and antiblockade.
summary: This paper models a 1D chain of Rydberg atoms interacting via constrained four-body forces, simulating non-thermal dynamics. By comparing a simplified kinetic model to the full interacting model, the authors show that the four-body term fundamentally alters the system's dynamics, leading to persistent quantum scars and long-range correlations. This provides a pathway to study controlled non-ergodic behavior using advanced Rydberg array platforms.
main_problem: The study investigates non-thermal dynamics and weak ergodicity breaking in a one-dimensional chain of Rydberg atoms subjected to constrained four-body interactions.
main_result: The inclusion of the state-dependent four-body interaction reverses the dynamics observed in the simpler kinetic model, causing the initial state $|0angle$ to develop long-range correlations while the system remains non-ergodic.
method: The authors employed an ansatz for the many-body ground state to diagonalize the Hamiltonian, deriving an effective low-energy model and analyzing time evolution using quantum many-body scar diagnostics.
model_or_system: The system is a 1D chain of Rydberg atoms realized in a Peierls array with alternating bond lengths, governed by a kinetically constrained Hamiltonian involving four-body interactions.
key_observables: Ground state energy scaling ($E_0 \propto L$), bipartite entanglement entropy, site-resolved occupation ($\langle Q_j angle$), and state revival dynamics.
important_parameters: The four-body interaction strength, the alternating bond lengths (related to blockade/antiblockade), and the chain length $L$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on developing a specific ansatz for the many-body ground state and approximating the full Hamiltonian via Schrieffer–Wolff transformations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the constrained interaction, ground state properties (energy, occupation, entanglement), and time evolution dynamics for different initial states ($|0angle$ vs $|Z_4angle$) under the kinetic term only versus the full model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the constrained four-body Hamiltonian, simplifying it using approximations (RWA, anti-blockade), deriving an effective Hamiltonian, and then analyzing the resulting dynamics and ground state properties by comparing the results from the simplified kinetic model versus the full interacting model.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the control of non-equilibrium quantum dynamics by engineering higher-order, state-dependent interactions (four-body) using Rydberg blockade/antiblockade mechanisms, which is a major frontier in AMO physics.
